result:
The proposed answer of 5 is wrong. The solution's own computation for $n=5$ gives a counterexample.

For $n=5$, take digits $d_1=4$, $d_2=4$, $d_3=-4$ (all in $D_5$, with the rest zero). Then $w=1/c$ satisfies $1+4w+4w^2-4w^3=0$, i.e. $4w^3-4w^2-4w-1=0$. Its real root is $r\approx 1.6824$, and the complex pair has $|w|^2=\tfrac{1/4}{r}\approx 0.1486<1$. So the complex roots give $c=1/w$ with $|c|>1$ and $c\notin\mathbb{R}$, meaning $c\in M_5\setminus\mathbb{R}$. Computing $w\approx -0.341\pm 0.179i$ and $|c-1|^2=\dfrac{|1-w|^2}{|w|^2}\approx 12.3 > 10 = 2n$. Hence $|c-1|\ge\sqrt{10}$, so $c\notin X_5$, and $M_5\setminus\mathbb{R}\not\subset X_5$.

The proposed solution itself notes that this cubic gives $|c-1|^2\approx 12.3>10$, but then asserts without justification that $n=5$ works. The claimed "verification" for $n=5$ is not an argument. So the answer cannot be 5. (I have not determined the correct value.)

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
